## Part A - Arithmetic Operations
```{r}
a <- 17
b <- 5
a + b
a - b
a * b
a /b
```
```{r}
 a %% b
a %/% b
```
```{r}
2 ^ 10
```
```{r}
17/5
17 %% 5
17 %/%5
```
## Question 1- 17/5 gives 3.4, 17 %% 5 gives the remainder of 2 while 17 %/%5 gives the whole number of 3.They are related because 17/5 is 3 and return the remainder 2.

## Question 2- The output of 10 %% 3 is 1 and the output of 10 %/% 3 is 3. The first gives the remainder while the second gives the whole number quotient.

## Part B Basic Data Types

```{r}
x <- 42
y <- 42L
z <- "42"
w <- TRUE
v <- 3 + 21

typeof(x)
typeof(y)
typeof(z)
typeof(w)
typeof(v)
```

## Question 3 -x <- 42 is stored as a double by default, while y <- 42L is explicitly stored as an integer. The L tells R to treat the number as an integer.

## Question 4 Yes. typeof(), class(), and mode() can give different answers because they describe different aspects of an object. For example, x has typeof(x) as "double", but class(x) and mode(x) are both "numeric".


## Part C- Type Conversion

```{r}
num_string <- "123"
num_value <- as.numeric(num_string)

typeof(num_value)
class(num_value)
mode(num_value)
```
```{r}
as.logical(0)
as.logical(1)
```
```{r}
bad_string <- "hello123"
as.numeric (bad_string)
```
## Question 5 - R gives a warning and returns NA because it cannot convert "hello123" into a valid number. R continues running so that the rest of the code can still execute.

## If warnings are ignored, NA values may cause incorrect or missing results without being noticed

## Question 6 -I think as.logical(2) will produce TRUE, while as.logical(-1) will also produce TRUE.


## Part D - Strings, phase() and paste()
```{r}
first_name <- "Krystal"
last_name <- "Catequista"

print(first_name)
print(last_name)
cat(first_name, last_name)
```
```{r}
full_name <- paste(first_name, last_name)
full_name0 <- paste0(first_name, last_name)

full_name
full_name0

```
